findings.description: Tier 0 pre-filter uses a fixed senior token regex to instantly reject postings if candidateProfile.no_senior is set. It also extracts numeric YOE via regex (matchAll) and rejects if the parsed floor exceeds candidate max_yoe by > 3 years.
findings.business_impact: Causes premature false rejections of viable junior/mid roles that contain words like 'architect' or 'lead' in non-senior contexts. Misreads preferred YOE or project experience as hard minimums.
failure_modes: False reject on non-senior titles containing 'architect' or 'lead'
Regex fails to distinguish preferred YOE from mandatory YOE
Fails on non-English YOE phrasing or Roman numerals
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts holistic seniority level and YOE requirements with context (mandatory vs preferred). Deterministic policy evaluates candidate max_yoe against the structured extraction.
findings.evidence:
const seniorRegex = /\b(senior|staff|principal|lead|director|vp|head of|architect)\b/i;
if (seniorRegex.test(title)) return { passed: false, reason: 'SENIOR_TITLE_FILTERED' };

findings.description: Restricts all job classification to a closed list of 10 static role families. Any emerging role (e.g. AI Product Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Agentic Systems Engineer) is forced into 'other' or misclassified into generic buckets.
findings.business_impact: Suppresses recall and misaligns candidate archetypes. Emergent AI engineering titles lose their domain distinction and get degraded in downstream matching.
failure_modes: Emergent AI engineering sub-disciplines forced into 'other'
Coarse granularity prevents nuanced archetype alignment
findings.recommended_target: System 1 ROLE_FAMILY_CLASSIFICATION produces hierarchical role concepts with primary family, sub-specialty, and archetype similarity score.

findings.description: System 1 extraction schema enforces structured fields, and escalates to System 2 when confidence < 0.85, alternative_qualifications === true, or ambiguous_yoe === true. Evidence quotes are validated via substring inclusion in lowercased JD text.
findings.business_impact: Fixed 0.85 confidence threshold is uncalibrated against human ground truth; arbitrary threshold causes either excess System 2 latency or missed ambiguities.
failure_modes: Model self-reported confidence is not calibrated to true accuracy
Over-escalation on benign alternative qualifications
findings.recommended_target: Keep escalation gate deterministic in code, but calibrate thresholds empirically via the evaluation corpus (Phase 19).

findings.description: Sanitizes untrusted job descriptions by escaping closing tags and pseudo-system tokens (e.g. </untrusted_job_description>, [system], <<SYS>>) before passing them into model prompts.
findings.business_impact: Prevents prompt injection and instruction override from adversarial job descriptions. Core security boundary.
failure_modes: New prompt injection delimiters not in escape list
Markdown formatting disruption if over-escaped
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic sanitization; augment with strict structural separation (system prompt vs user message data isolation).

findings.description: Rejects job if title contains any senior keyword, regardless of the job's actual responsibilities or requirements.
findings.business_impact: Rejects junior or associate roles that contain 'lead' or 'head' in phrasing, or roles where title is elevated but actual YOE requirement is 1-2 years.
failure_modes: False negative on inflated titles with entry-level requirements
Misses non-English senior markers (e.g., Hebrew 'בכיר')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts holistic seniority level and evidence; deterministic candidate fit gate in code evaluates candidate profile fit rules.

findings.description: Scans JD text with regexes looking for phrases demanding work authorization, security clearance, or citizenship.
findings.business_impact: Critical legal requirements can be missed if phrased colloquially, or falsely triggered on affirmative sponsorship statements ('we provide visa sponsorship').
failure_modes: Falsely triggers on 'we offer visa sponsorship' or 'sponsorship available'
Misses alternative legal phrasings ('EU passport holders only', 'Israeli ID required')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts legal requirements and quoted spans; deterministic code checks candidate verified facts and routes unknown facts to NEEDS_REVIEW.

findings.description: Normalizes degree strings (BSc, BA, MSc, MA, PhD) using regex string replacements and compares extracted field of study by stripping generic education words.
findings.business_impact: Inability to understand degree equivalence causes unwarranted NEEDS_REVIEW or REJECT.
failure_modes: Fails on international degree names (e.g. Israeli Practical Engineer, European Bologna degrees)
Strict field string stripping fails on related disciplines (Math/Physics vs CS)
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts degree level, field, and equivalence clauses; deterministic policy checks candidate degree records with explicit human review on ambiguous equivalence.

findings.description: Implements candidate fit policy: shortfall >= 4 years => REJECT; shortfall > 0 => LONG_STRETCH; preferred shortfall => REASONABLE; no shortfall => STRONG. Requires fact provenance in primary sources (cv.md, profile.yml).
findings.example: if (shortfall >= 4) return { status: 'REJECT' }; if (shortfall > 0) return { status: 'LONG_STRETCH' };
findings.business_impact: Core business logic enforcing candidate's early-career targeting. Must remain deterministic and transparent.
failure_modes: Rigid boundaries if input YOE was mis-extracted by upstream layer
Constants hardcoded in function rather than loaded from candidate profile policy
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic decision policy in code ('Code Decides'). Feed it clean, structured semantic evidence from System 1.
findings.evidence: const shortfall = extracted.required_yoe - years; if (shortfall >= 4) return { status: 'REJECT' };

findings.description: Classifies ATS form field inputs into 24 predefined semantic types using cascading regex tests over field labels and names.
findings.business_impact: Misclassifying an ATS question leads to incorrect field mapping or inappropriate DO_NOT_ANSWER.
failure_modes: Multilingual ATS form labels completely fail detection
Subtle phrasing differences misclassify sensitive fields
findings.recommended_target: System 1 classifies field intent with confidence and quoted span; deterministic code enforces DO_NOT_ANSWER on sensitive/legal fields.
findings.evidence: export function semanticTypeFor(label = '', name = '') { const sponsorship = /\b(visa|sponsorship...)/... }

findings.description: Detects legal attestations, terms, background checks, demographic (EEO), and sensitive personal questions using broad regex keyword matching.
findings.business_impact: Safety boundary preventing automated answering of legal attestations and sensitive demographic disclosures.
failure_modes: Unfamiliar legal phrases fail detection, risking auto-answering sensitive fields
Benign technical questions containing 'background' or 'condition' falsely marked sensitive
findings.recommended_target: System 1 semantic classification of question intent, coupled with a deterministic fail-closed safety policy that flags any uncertain question for human review.
findings.evidence: if (/\b(i agree|i certify|i attest|consent|authorize|terms and conditions...)\b/i.test(label)) return 'LEGAL_ATTESTATION';

findings.description: Deterministically maps candidate facts to classified ATS fields. Enforces that sensitive fields return DO_NOT_ANSWER, requires source-backed facts for all values, and verifies GPA scales before proposing values.
findings.business_impact: Guarantees no hallucinated candidate data or automated answers to sensitive legal questions. Critical ethical boundary.
failure_modes: Rigid scale matching rejects valid GPA conversions
Cannot handle multi-part address or date formatting
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic mapping policy in code ('Code Decides'). Rely on System 1 only for semantic input classification.

findings.description: Scores CV bullets for reordering by checking if bullet text contains extracted JD keywords via string .includes(), adding +3 points per match.
findings.business_impact: Primitive keyword matching rewards superficial keyword stuffing and fails to detect genuine conceptual relevance or achievement alignment.
failure_modes: Partial substring false positives (e.g. 'go' matching 'algorithm')
Ignores semantic equivalence and conceptual depth
findings.recommended_target: System 1 CANDIDATE_CAPABILITY_EXTRACTION and REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATE_MATCH to score bullet relevance based on semantic capability match.

findings.description: Compiles 'word:' and 'stem:' prefixed title filter keywords into Unicode-aware regular expressions. Uses a custom negative lookaround WORD_CHAR pattern excluding CJK/Hangul scripts so Latin terms match on word boundaries without requiring whitespace in East Asian text.
findings.business_impact: Ensures zero-token scanner performs exact boundary filtering without regex crashes on international titles.
failure_modes: Cannot handle hyphenated or slash-separated compound roles (e.g. 'ML/AI')
Overlooks morphology in inflected languages
findings.recommended_target: Retain as fast deterministic pre-filter in zero-token portal scanner.

findings.description: Auto-anchors short keywords (2-3 characters) with word boundaries to prevent substring collisions (e.g. 'ai' in 'chair' or 'vp' in 'devops'). Longer terms fall back to raw substring search unless explicitly prefixed.
findings.business_impact: Heuristic boundary rule that leaks false positives on longer words while causing false drops on short hyphenated acronyms.
failure_modes: Substrings like 'java' matching 'javascript'
Compound terms with punctuation behaving unpredictably
findings.recommended_target: Retain in zero-token scanner; semantic discovery and triage should handle conceptual matching.

findings.description: Hard-coded sets of seniority tokens used during tracker deduplication to decide if two job titles describe the same role level.
findings.business_impact: If an employer uses nonstandard seniority words, dedup either falsely merges distinct reqs or creates duplicate rows.
failure_modes: Fails on localized/foreign seniority descriptors
Treats 'Lead' as seniority even when referring to technical focus ('Tech Lead')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 JOB_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_COMPARISON to determine role equivalence during deduplication.

findings.description: Parses Roman (I-VI) and Arabic (1-6) numerals to distinguish leveled role variants (e.g. 'Software Engineer I' vs 'Software Engineer II') in tracker deduplication.
findings.business_impact: Prevents merging different leveled openings at the same company. Important structural distinction.
failure_modes: Collides with version numbers (e.g. 'Web3', 'Vue 3', 'Python 3')
Fails on levels above 6 (e.g. Google L7, Meta E7)
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic level parsing for explicit numerals, but use System 1 to resolve semantic leveling in complex titles.

findings.description: Static set of 60+ stopwords covering seniority, contract mode (remote, fulltime), job nouns (position, team), locations (London, Berlin, Bangalore), and regions.
findings.business_impact: Stopwords stripped before Jaccard calculation. Missing locations inflate false dissimilarities; unlisted generic words cause false duplicate merges.
failure_modes: Unlisted cities (e.g. Tel Aviv, Herzliya) treated as role identity tokens
Drops meaningful domain terms if they collide with geographic names
findings.recommended_target: System 1 role and entity parsing separates title core from location, work mode, and level metadata.

findings.description: Replaces 'Member of Technical Staff' with 'engineer' to prevent titles from failing fuzzy match due to company-specific boilerplate prefixes.
findings.business_impact: Handles Silicon Valley title convention, but is a bespoke patch for one specific title pattern.
failure_modes: Fails on other corporate title prefixes (e.g. 'Individual Contributor', 'Associate Member', 'Fellow')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts canonical role function regardless of corporate title scaffolding.

findings.description: Lists discriminating short acronyms (api, sre, sdk, gpu, ios, qa) and generic baseline tokens (software, engineer, developer, platform) that cannot be the sole reason two titles match.
findings.business_impact: Bespoke heuristics to tune Jaccard similarity across role titles in tracker merges.
failure_modes: Missing short acronyms (e.g. 'llm', 'rag', 'ev', 'db') get stripped by length filter
Rigid token matching misses synonymous domains ('data platform' vs 'data infrastructure')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 semantic similarity comparison for job deduplication.

findings.description: Calculates Jaccard token overlap between two titles. Enforces rules: must have >= 2 overlapping tokens; baseline-only overlap rejected; sub-baseline seniority mismatch rejected; leveled numerals mismatch rejected.
findings.business_impact: Drives application tracker deduplication. False match overwrites distinct job rows; false mismatch creates duplicate tracker entries.
failure_modes: Fails on inverted titles ('Backend Engineer, Payments' vs 'Payments - Software Engineer')
Fails on cross-lingual title variations
findings.recommended_target: Hybrid deduplication: deterministic req ID / URL keys first; System 1 JOB_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_COMPARISON for ambiguous titles; fail-safe to keeping both rows on uncertainty.

findings.description: Hard-coded array of ~100 technology names compiled into a single giant regular expression (SKILL_PATTERN) to extract technical skills from job descriptions and CVs.
findings.business_impact: Blind to any library, framework, or tool not explicitly listed in the 100-item array. Directly distorts upskill gap analysis and pattern reporting.
failure_modes: Unlisted modern tools (e.g. LangGraph, Polars, vLLM, SGLang, Qdrant) are completely invisible
Case variations or hyphenations not in regex are missed
findings.recommended_target: System 1 SKILL_EXTRACTION & SKILL_NORMALIZATION based on contextual capability extraction, not a static keyword dictionary.

findings.description: Dictionary mapping common abbreviations and spelling variations to a canonical display name.
findings.business_impact: Hand-authored alias dictionary requires continuous manual updates. Misses relationships between adjacent frameworks or ecosystem evolutions.
failure_modes: Cannot handle semantic equivalence (e.g. 'FastAPI' implying 'Python Backend')
Omitted variations cause duplicate skills in gap analysis
findings.recommended_target: System 1 SKILL_NORMALIZATION mapping surface forms to canonical SkillConcept entities with relation types (EXACT, EQUIVALENT, TRANSFERABLE).

findings.description: Regexes designed to catch certifications (e.g. AWS Certified) or AI 'fine-tuning' while filtering out non-technical verb uses ('fine-tune campaign spend').
findings.business_impact: Fragile regular expressions attempting natural language disambiguation of verb vs noun phrases.
failure_modes: Fails on rephrased certifications ('Certified Kubernetes Administrator')
False triggers or misses on nuanced AI modeling prose
findings.recommended_target: System 1 SKILL_EXTRACTION distinguishes technology use, certification, and conceptual knowledge contextually.

findings.description: 2D array of static synonym pairs (e.g. ['js', 'javascript'], ['ts', 'typescript'], ['nlp', 'natural language processing']) used for ATS keyword coverage calculation.
findings.business_impact: Keyword coverage check in ATS preparation under-reports match percentage whenever candidate uses equivalent terms not in this 30-entry table.
failure_modes: Rigid binary pairs cannot express directional or partial overlap
Fails on modern acronyms (RAG, CoT, LoRA)
findings.recommended_target: System 1 SKILL_NORMALIZATION & REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATE_MATCH with relation taxonomy (EQUIVALENT, STRONG_RELATED, TRANSFERABLE).

findings.description: Array of regex patterns to locate requirement sections in report markdown files (e.g. /##\s*(?:required|technical)\s*requirements/i).
findings.business_impact: Locates requirement sections in evaluation reports. Misses sections if formatted slightly differently in non-standard templates.
failure_modes: Fails on non-English report headings
Misses inline bullet requirement headers
findings.recommended_target: Keep markdown structural heading parser; supplement with System 1 section classification if report format varies.

findings.description: Calculates percentage of JD keywords present in CV text; categorizes each keyword as present (count >= 2), thin (count === 1), or missing (count === 0).
findings.business_impact: ATS diagnostic tool. Pure lexical counting rewards keyword density over genuine technical capability.
failure_modes: Counts repeated occurrences without evaluating relevance
Treats passing mentions the same as core professional achievements
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic coverage diagnostic for raw ATS keyword check; do not use as candidate fit score.
findings.evidence: return { total: keywords.length, present: present.length, thin: thin.length, missing: missing.length, score };

findings.description: Extracts candidate skills from JD bullets by matching any capitalized word or technical token (starting with [A-Z]) that contains alphanumerics and symbols (+, #, .).
findings.business_impact: Extracts non-skills like 'Deep', 'Proven', 'Passion' or city names if not caught by STOPWORDS. Completely misses lowercase skills ('bash', 'git', 'sql', 'rest api').
failure_modes: Misses all lowercase technical skills
Captures sentence-opening capitalized English words as phantom skills
findings.recommended_target: System 1 SKILL_EXTRACTION from requirement text.

findings.description: Massive hand-maintained stopword list designed to prevent capitalized sentence starters and degree/seniority words from being misidentified as skills by SKILL_TOKEN_RE.
findings.business_impact: Symptom of compensating for a broken regex heuristic with an ever-expanding blacklist.
failure_modes: New capitalized adjectives continuously generate phantom skill gaps
Legitimate technologies that collide with common words get dropped
findings.recommended_target: Replace regex + stopword filter with System 1 SKILL_EXTRACTION.

findings.description: Classifies each extracted JD skill against candidate's CV as 'existing', 'supportedByResume', or 'gap' using exact string and CANONICAL alias matches.
findings.example: if (cvSkills.has(norm)) return 'existing'; if (canonical && cvSkills.has(canonical)) return 'supportedByResume'; return 'gap';
findings.business_impact: Reports false skill gaps when candidate has transferable or related skills, biasing candidate away from good opportunities.
failure_modes: FastAPI vs Python backend marked as gap
LangGraph vs Agent Orchestration marked as gap
PostgreSQL vs Relational Database marked as gap
findings.recommended_target: System 1 REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATE_MATCH producing relationship classes (EXACT, EQUIVALENT, TRANSFERABLE, GAP).

findings.description: Ranks STAR interview stories against a job posting by counting shared non-stopword tokens between the JD text and story descriptions.
findings.business_impact: Selects interview prep stories based on superficial word repetition rather than relevant technical challenge or architectural scope.
failure_modes: Selects story that repeats common JD words instead of story demonstrating core required competency
findings.recommended_target: System 1 matches candidate STAR achievements to job requirements based on capability relevance.

findings.description: Extracts currency symbols ($/€/£/₪), numerical compensation values, and intervals (hourly, monthly, yearly, k-suffix) from job postings and reports.
findings.business_impact: Parses compensation ranges for compensation gap calculation and salary benchmarking.
failure_modes: Misinterprets non-compensation numbers (e.g. '100k requests/sec')
Fails on complex multi-currency equity/bonus structures
findings.recommended_target: System 1 identifies the compensation text snippet; deterministic parser extracts numbers and standardizes currencies.

findings.description: Normalizes location strings to tax/cost-of-living jurisdictions (US, UK, DE, IL, Remote) for market salary benchmarking.
findings.business_impact: Ensures salary comparison is made against the right local market.
failure_modes: Misclassifies multi-country remote roles
Misses regional variations in large countries
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts location and work model constraints; deterministic code maps jurisdiction to salary benchmarks.

findings.description: Parses explicit `**Provenance:**` tags in story-bank.md to enforce the four-tier trust model (`cv.md`, `user-stated`, `derived-unverified`, `user-cannot-confirm`). Prevents unverified scale claims from polluting generated CVs.
findings.business_impact: Guarantees that AI-generated interview prep numbers do not leak into CV factuality claims. Critical anti-fabrication boundary.
failure_modes: Malformed markdown tag syntax ignored
Untagged entries default to derived-unverified
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic parsing and enforcement of provenance tags. Never let an LLM override `user-cannot-confirm`.

findings.description: Regular expressions matching Experience, Education, Skills, and Summary section headings across 18 languages to evaluate CV parseability for ATS parsers.
findings.business_impact: ATS parseability verification. If a candidate uses an unlisted heading variation, ATS score is falsely penalized.
failure_modes: Unlisted localized headings trigger parseability warnings
Creative headings ('Where I\'ve Built') rejected as unparseable
findings.recommended_target: Retain core deterministic heading regexes for strict ATS compliance; allow System 1 to verify section semantics for modern parsers.

findings.description: Inspects generated CV HTML for tables, multi-column CSS grids, non-standard fonts, text selection, and contrast that break legacy ATS text extraction.
findings.business_impact: Ensures generated PDFs parse cleanly in older ATS engines (Workday, Taleo).
failure_modes: Flags benign CSS styling that modern ATS parsers handle correctly
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic HTML/PDF structural checks.
findings.evidence: if (/<table/i.test(html)) issues.push('Tables in CV layout break ATS linear reading order');

findings.description: Whitelists and blacklists prose words to stop tool-of-trade conflation (e.g. 'using Java' vs 'built Java') and prevent common English nouns from triggering false tool-authorship violations.
findings.business_impact: Enforces non-negotiable rule: 'NEVER claim the user authored a tool/library unless explicitly attributed in cv.md'.
failure_modes: Uncommon English nouns mistaken for proprietary tools
Complex grammatical structures evade regex authorship checks
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic authorship and metric verification gate. Never replace with an LLM self-audit.

findings.description: Extracts all numbers, percentages, dollar amounts, and metric scales from generated CV text and verifies that each exact number exists in cv.md or article-digest.md.
findings.business_impact: Zero tolerance for fabricated metrics (e.g. turning 'improved latency' into 'improved latency by 45%').
failure_modes: Reformatted numbers falsely flagged as ungrounded
Date ranges mistaken for metrics if not excluded
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic verbatim number grounding gate.

findings.description: Checks that tailored CV JSON payload preserves the canonical `· {descriptor}` suffix on job titles and maintains experience entries in exact reverse chronological order matching cv.md.
findings.business_impact: Prevents AI CV generator from silently dropping title descriptors or scrambling employment timeline.
failure_modes: Non-standard title separators not recognized as descriptors
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic structural integrity validator.

findings.description: Compares each job title in the tailored CV payload against the canonical title in cv.md for the same company and dates. Normalizes whitespace and casing, but forbids title rewrites.
findings.business_impact: Prevents AI from exaggerating a job title (e.g. changing 'Junior Developer' to 'Senior AI Architect') during CV generation.
failure_modes: Company name variations prevent pairing
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic title consistency validator.

findings.description: Builds regex to filter job postings by candidate's allowed countries from portals.yml location filter.
findings.business_impact: Discards postings from jurisdictions where candidate has no work authorization or relocation interest.
failure_modes: Fails on localized city names without country code
False drops on worldwide remote postings that do not list countries explicitly
findings.recommended_target: Retain fast regex pre-filter in zero-token scanner; System 1 WORK_MODEL_EXTRACTION verifies ambiguous location clauses.

findings.description: Scans job text in portal scanner for hard no-sponsorship signals (e.g. 'no visa sponsorship', 'must be US citizen').
findings.business_impact: Zero-token drop of jobs candidate cannot legally hold.
failure_modes: Regex false-positive on 'no visa sponsorship required for this role'
Misses complex European or Israeli legal eligibility terms
findings.recommended_target: Fast veto regex in scanner; System 1 extracts precise legal eligibility during hydration.

findings.description: Extracts compensation from scanner preview snippets and drops postings below candidate's minimum salary floor.
findings.business_impact: Filters out underpaid roles before token expenditure.
failure_modes: Fails on non-standard rate periods
Drops roles where equity or bonus is primary comp
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic filter for explicit numbers; System 1 extracts complex comp structures.

findings.description: Applies compiled positive and negative regular expressions from title-keywords.mjs against posting title.
findings.business_impact: First line of defense in zero-token portal scanner.
failure_modes: Negative keywords over-drop legitimate roles
Positive keywords constrain discovery recall
findings.recommended_target: Keep fast deterministic filter in zero-token scan; augment discovery with System 1 query expansion.

findings.description: Extracts requisition numbers (e.g. 'req JR-10423', 'job id 88214', 'ref R_2291') and normalizes posting URLs to serve as deterministic deduplication keys.
findings.business_impact: Prevents duplicate application rows when requisition IDs match. Deterministic identity anchor.
failure_modes: Fails on requisition IDs with non-standard prefix formats
Aggregator URLs often hide the employer req ID
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic URL and Req ID extraction as primary dedup key ('Code Decides').

findings.description: Strips tracking parameters (utm_*, gh_src), lowercases host, normalizes trailing slashes, and preserves SPA job hash routes (#/job/123).
findings.business_impact: Ensures URL identity is completely canonical across disparate sources and web scrapers.
failure_modes: Custom tracking params not in strip list
Regional subdomain differences on aggregator boards
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic URL normalization. Never use model inference for URL canonicalization.

findings.description: Multi-tier deduplication cascade: 1) Normalized URL match, 2) Req ID in notes match, 3) Report number match, 4) Fuzzy company + role match via role-matcher.mjs.
findings.example: if (urlMatch) updateRow(); else if (reqMatch) updateRow(); else if (fuzzyMatch) updateRow(); else insertRow();
findings.business_impact: Controls whether an incoming job is merged into an existing row or creates a new row. Tier 4 fuzzy match is brittle.
failure_modes: Tier 4 fuzzy title match erroneously folds two distinct team requisitions into one row
findings.recommended_target: Tiers 1-3 remain deterministic; Tier 4 uses System 1 JOB_DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_COMPARISON with fail-safe to insert separate rows on uncertainty.

findings.description: Flags roles re-listed 2+ times in 90 days from scan-history.tsv. Requires 2+ distinct URLs seen on 2+ distinct scan dates with identical normalized title.
findings.example: reposts = history.filter(h => h.company === c && h.normalizedTitle === t && h.dateDiff > 0)
findings.business_impact: Identifies stale/ghost openings re-posted repeatedly without hiring. Block G legitimacy signal.
failure_modes: Misses reposts if company tweaked title slightly ('AI Engineer' -> 'Applied AI Engineer')
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic scan ledger analysis; allow System 1 semantic duplicate comparison to catch slightly modified repost titles.

findings.description: Fuzzy-matches pasted interview invite email against tracker rows based on company name, role title tokens, date proximity, and requisition ID.
findings.business_impact: Links incoming interview invitations to tracked applications for automated status updates and prep doc creation.
failure_modes: Ambiguous company names in email signatures cause wrong row linkage
Heuristic point weights fail on multiple concurrent applications to the same company
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts company, role, recruiter, and req ID from unstructured invite text; deterministic code updates tracker state.

findings.description: Classifies recruiter/company emails into REJECTION, INTERVIEW_INVITE, ASSESSMENT, or ACKNOWLEDGEMENT using regex keyword matching over email subject and body.
findings.business_impact: Suggests tracker updates. Moving tracker state directly from regex without human review risks premature rejection or skipped interviews.
failure_modes: Misinterprets polite rejection as positive update or vice versa
Fails on non-English recruiter replies
findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts reply intent and evidence; human operator authorizes tracker status change ('Humans Authorize').
findings.evidence: if (/\b(unfortunately|regret to inform|not moving forward)\b/i.test(body)) return 'REJECTION';

findings.description: Uses Hebrew regex /היברידי|מרחוק/i to classify job location strings on Israeli tech board Geektime Insider as 'Hybrid / Remote'.
findings.business_impact: Directly impacts work-model tagging for Israeli tech jobs. Hand-crafted regex fails on other Hebrew variations ('עבודה מהבית', 'היברידית', 'משולב').
failure_modes: Misses Hebrew phrases like 'עבודה מהבית' (work from home) or 'מודל משולב' (hybrid model)
findings.recommended_target: System 1 WORK_MODEL_EXTRACTION with multilingual Hebrew/English support.

findings.description: Uses German keyword regex to detect remote work in German federal employment agency (Arbeitsagentur) postings.
findings.business_impact: Filters German public sector job feed for remote opportunities.
failure_modes: Misses compound German nouns ('Homeoffice-Möglichkeit', 'ortsunabhängig')
findings.recommended_target: System 1 WORK_MODEL_EXTRACTION with German language support.

findings.description: Matches facet field names in Workday ATS JSON responses to find location/country/region checkboxes.
findings.business_impact: Structural navigation of Workday search API facets.
failure_modes: Changes to Workday JSON schema facet names
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic JSON facet identifier.

findings.description: Maps careers URLs to specific ATS adapters (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters) based on exact hostname and path regexes.
findings.business_impact: Determines which scraper / API adapter fetches postings. Deterministic infrastructure router.
failure_modes: Custom domains hiding ATS vendor unless CNAME/DOM inspected
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic URL regex routing ('Code Decides').

findings.description: Classifies tracker job rows in the web dashboard into 'Senior' vs 'Junior / Entry' using static regexes on role title.
findings.business_impact: Analytics dashboard charts diverge from agent domain classification because web UI maintains an independent duplicate keyword list.
failure_modes: Diverges from src/agent/domain/jobs/job-evaluator.mjs and role-matcher.mjs
Duplicated intelligence creates inconsistent statistics
findings.recommended_target: Consume canonical JobSemanticProfile.seniority produced by System 1 instead of hand-rolling UI regexes.

findings.description: Finds which option of an open combobox menu matches an answer by checking exact label or unique whole-word match to prevent substring accidents.
findings.business_impact: Prevents wrong option selection in ATS comboboxes. High-integrity UI selector.
failure_modes: Multiple options containing same keyword return -1 (leave for human)
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic word boundary option picker.

findings.description: Matches generated PDF artifacts in output/ by slug and token delimiters to ensure the right tailored CV or cover letter is served for each company.
findings.business_impact: Prevents serving the wrong candidate's CV or wrong company's tailored PDF. High-integrity file resolver.
failure_modes: Slug collisions if two companies share identical short stems
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic filename slug matcher.
findings.evidence: export function hasToken(filenameLower, token) { ... return re.test(filenameLower); }

findings.description: Filters application tracker rows in the Go terminal dashboard using strings.Contains and canonical status mapping.
findings.business_impact: UI presentation only. Does not alter business state or evaluation scores.
failure_modes: Basic substring search cannot handle typo tolerance
findings.recommended_target: Keep deterministic TUI text filtering.

findings.description: Qualitative assessment of posting authenticity: Tier 1 (Verified Direct), Tier 2 (Likely Active), Tier 3 (Stale/Aggregator), Tier 4 (Ghost/Suspicious). Evaluates freshness, direct vs aggregator, repost history, and ATS presence.
findings.example: Tier 1: Fresh direct employer posting on first-party ATS board

findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts company presence and hiring signals; deterministic code combines liveness, repost history, and aggregator status into legitimacy tier.

findings.description: Specialized market rules for Israeli high-tech: recognition of IDF technological intelligence units (8200, Matzov, Mamram, Talpiot), local compensation norms (Keren Hishtalmut, 10Bis, gross monthly ILS), Hebrew tech terms, and local startup stages.
findings.example: Military technological unit service maps to 2-4 years professional equivalent experience
findings.business_impact: Essential for accurate candidate matching in the Israeli tech ecosystem, where military tech experience is equivalent to senior engineering.

findings.recommended_target: System 1 extracts military tech unit context and Hebrew terms; deterministic code validates candidate primary facts and computes equivalent experience.
